note.question: Should an owner place two projects inside one multidivisional firm or separate firms when managers privately learn profitability and disclosure is costly?
note.overview: A founder selects a multidivisional or stand-alone organization before privately informed managers decide whether to disclose project profitability and competitive investors decide how much capital to provide. Beliefs, financing, disclosure, and internal allocation are jointly determined in Perfect Bayesian equilibrium.

components.label: Perfect Bayesian equilibrium with investment-efficiency selection
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Perfect Bayesian equilibrium with investment-efficiency selection. Managers' disclosure and allocation choices and investors' financing choices are sequentially optimal given beliefs; investor beliefs satisfy Bayes' rule on path. If the model admits multiple Perfect Bayesian equilibria, the paper selects the equilibrium producing the greatest investment efficiency.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At date 0 the founder chooses a multidivisional firm or two stand-alone firms. At date 1 the relevant manager or managers observe binary project profitability and choose whether to make truthful costly disclosures. At date 2 competitive investors observe disclosures and choose capital and break-even ownership shares. At date 3, if a multidivisional firm receives only one unit, its manager allocates that unit across projects.
